We need to implement function `relocateMarbles` that given list of initial positions `nums`, moves defined by moveFrom and moveTo arrays: at each step i, move all marbles at position moveFrom[i] to position moveTo[i]. We need to return sorted list of empty positions after all moves.

Constraints: numbers up to 1e9, length up to 1e5. Must be efficient (O(n log n)). We cannot simulate each position's count with huge array.

We need to keep track of positions that currently have marbles, with counts (since there may be multiple marbles). Since we need to compute empty positions after all moves: any position that never ends up having any marbles is considered empty (including those that had marbles originally but later moved away and never get any again, also positions that never had any marbles at all).

But the universe of positions is huge (up to 1e9) but number of distinct positions referenced (in nums, moveFrom, moveTo) is O(n). However empty positions also include many positions not in these sets (any position not referenced anywhere). For example, in Example 1, positions 3,4 are not in initial or move lists but are empty. Actually they are empty because no marbles ever go there; they also never were referenced. They are infinite. But they expect to output only certain positions: they return [1,3,4,5,7,8,9]. Output is [1,3,4,5,7,8,9] includes positions 3,4 which are not in union set.
